Fill button 1 Fill button 2 Fill button 3 Maximum bolus Maximum basal rate This value is called max basal in OpenAPS context Max IOB for SMB This value is called Max IOB in OpenAPS context\nOpenAPS will not add more insulin if current IOB is greater than this value. Value is affected by patient type too. Max IOB for AMA This value is called Max IOB in OpenAPS context\nThis is maximal insulin in [U] APS can deliver at once. Value is affected by patient type too. Max daily safety multiplier Default value: 3 This is a key OpenAPS safety cap. What this does is limit your basals to be 3x (in this people) your biggest basal rate. You likely will not need to change this, but you should be aware that’s what is discussed about “3x max daily; 4x current” for safety caps. Current basal safety multiplier Default value: 4 This is the other half of the key OpenAPS safety caps, and the other half of “3x max daily; 4x current” of the safety caps. This means your basal, regardless of max basal set on your pump, cannot be any higher than this number times the current level of your basal. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting excessively high max basals before understanding how the algorithm works. Again, the default is 4x; most people will never need to adjust this and are instead more likely to need to adjust other settings if they feel like they are “running into” this safety cap. Bolus snooze DIA divisor Default value: 2\nBolus snooze is enacted after you do a meal bolus, so the loop won’t counteract with low temps when you’ve just eaten. The example here and default is 2; so a 3 hour DIA means that bolus snooze will be gradually phased out over 1.5 hours (3DIA/2). AMA min 5m carbs impact SMB min 5m carbs impact Default value: 3.0 (AMA) or 8.0 (SMB). This is a setting for default carb absorption impact per 5 minutes. The default is an expected 3mg/dl/5min. This affects how fast COB are decayed, and how much carb absorption is assumed in calculating future predicted BG, when BG is falling more than expected, or not rising as much as expected. Absorption cutoff Time at which any meal is considered absorbed. Remaining carbs will be cut off. Absorption max time Time in hours where is expected all carbs from meal will be absorbed Autosens min Default value: 0.7\nThe other side of the autosens safety limits, putting a cap on how low autosens can adjust basals, and how high it can adjust ISF and BG targets. Autosens max Default value: 1.2\nThis is a multiplier cap for autosens (and soon autotune) to set a 20%% max limit on how high the autosens ratio can be, which in turn determines how high autosens can adjust basals, how low it can adjust ISF, and how low it can set the BG target. AutoISF min (autoISF_min) Similar to autosens_min this defines how weak ISF can become.\n\nThe default value 1.0 effectively shuts off this effect. AutoISF max (autoISF_max) Similar to autosens_max this defines how strong ISF can become.\n\nThe default value 1.0 effectively shuts off this effect.\n\nWARNING: Be extremely careful when using values above 2.5 BG acceleration ISF weight (bgAccel_ISF_weight) This is the weight applied while glucose accelerates and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. BG brake ISF weight (bgBrake_ISF_weight) This is the weight applied while glucose decelerates and which weakens ISF thereby potentially reducing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. Low BG range weight (lower_ISFrange_weight) This is the weight applied while glucose is below target and which weakens ISF thereby potentially reducing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. High BG range weight (higher_ISFrange_weight) This is the weight applied while glucose is above target and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. SMB delivery ratio BG range (openapsama_smb_delivery_ratio_bg_range) Default value: 0. The linearly increasing SMB delivery ratio is mapped to the glucose range [target_bg, target_bg+bg_range].\nAt target_bg the SMB ratio is smb_delivery_ratio_min, at target_bg+bg_range it is smb_delivery_ratio_max\nWith 0 the linearly increasing SMB ratio is disabled and the fixed smb_delivery_ratio is used. Post-prandial ISF weight (pp_ISF_weight) This is the weight applied while glucose is rising and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. Duration ISF weight (dura_ISF_weight) This is the weight applied during longer lasting, elevated glucose plateaus and which strengthens ISF thereby potentially increasing insulin delivery.\n\nThe default value 0.0 effectively shuts off this effect. SMB delivery ratio (openapsama_smb_delivery_ratio) Default value: 0.5 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies what share of the total insulin required can be delivered as SMB. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting SMB requests from the caregivers phone at the same time. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution. SMB delivery ratio min (openapsama_smb_delivery_ratio_min) Default value: 0.5 This is the lower end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above. SMB delivery ratio max (openapsama_smb_delivery_ratio_max) Default value: 0.5 This is the upper end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above. SMB max range extension (openapsama_smb_max_range_extension) Default value: 1 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies by what factor you can exceed the regular 120 maxSMB/maxUAM minutes. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution.

AIMI Advisor: personal on-device risk model When you open Advisor, trains small models from recent loop+CGM features. Informational only; does not change insulin delivery. AI Coach: include structured OREF insights Adds a plain-language facts block for the coach LLM. Turn off for a shorter cloud prompt. Transient preference overlay (TPO) Temporarily lowers correction aggression for 45 min after post-hypo, poor sleep, or hyper→hypo exhaustion. Requires Control Center autonomy ≥ Assisted application. Reverts automatically. TPO: require LLM confirmation When on, AIMI applies a TPO session only if the advisor LLM confirms the clinical context (uses the same API keys as AI Coach). When off, algorithm triggers apply directly. TPO: notify on session start Shows a system notification when a 45 min protection session starts or ends. Tap to open OpenAPS AIMI preferences. Straight-line tube advisor (SMB caps) Discrete short-horizon control on max SMB: keeps predicted minimum BG above a floor using the PKPD min curve, favors larger caps when eventual BG is high, penalizes zig-zag SMB sizing. Does not replace PKPD or safety nets. Off by default. T3C: Autodrive basal authority Under T3C brittle mode, fuse Autodrive’s temporary basal demand with the T3C PI controller. SMB from Autodrive is never delivered (basal-only). The physiological tree can unlock a higher basal ceiling and faster ramp on a confirmed rise. Off disables fusion (PI-only + shadow Autodrive). T3C: Hyper basal floor Under T3C brittle mode, when glucose has stayed at or above 160 mg/dL for at least 20 minutes, hold the basal at your configured Max basal rate so sensor noise cannot collapse the correction to zero. Basal only (no SMB). Releases automatically once glucose falls back below 160 mg/dL. On by default. This is not medical advice — review your settings with your care team. T3C: CFRD mode Cystic fibrosis–related diabetes adaptations under T3C: higher LGS safety floor, delayed COB absorption for malabsorption, and inflammation-aware basal aggressiveness. Basal-only (no SMB). On by default when T3C brittle mode is used. This is not medical advice — review with your CF/diabetes care team. T3C CFRD: pulmonary exacerbation Manual flag for active pulmonary exacerbation or corticosteroid treatment. Raises the T3C basal aggressiveness ceiling while CFRD mode is on. Turn off when the exacerbation ends. Off by default. T3C CFRD: LGS safety floor Minimum LGS threshold (mg/dL) used by T3C anticipation when CFRD mode is on. Impaired counter-regulation needs a higher floor than typical T1D. Range 70–95. T3C CFRD: COB absorption delay Minutes to shift the COB prediction curve forward for delayed/irregular carbohydrate absorption. Feeds basal anticipation only (no SMB). Range 0–90 min. Enable Emergency SOS Send SMS with BG, trend, IOB and location when a severe hypo or missing CGM data is detected. SMS only (no automatic calls). Emergency contact #1 Primary phone number for SOS SMS (include country code, e.g. +33…). Emergency contact #2 Optional second contact. Identical numbers are deduplicated so only one SMS is sent. Monitoring threshold (30 min) BG (mg/dL) below which the 30-minute observation window starts. Recovery requires returning above this value + 10. Immediate emergency threshold BG (mg/dL) that triggers an immediate SOS SMS (also triggered when delta ≤ −10 mg/dL). Missing sensor alert (minutes) If no valid CGM reading is seen for this many minutes, send a missing-data SOS SMS. Undeclared-meal COB estimation Estimates virtual carbs from the glucose appearance rate (Ra), BG dynamics, patient weight/TDD and rest/activity context, then feeds them into the prediction curves so basal (TBR) anticipates an undeclared meal. Never delivers autonomous SMB. Automatically muted during exercise, hypo/post-hypo, pulmonary exacerbation and any stress/dawn false-meal suppression. Off by default. Undeclared COB: maximum grams Upper bound (grams) for the virtual carbs the estimator may inject into the prediction path. Lower = safer and smaller effect. Only used when undeclared-meal COB estimation is on. DynISF: trajectory tuning (CGM geometry) Uses the same short-horizon CGM features as AutoISF (deltas, parabolic projection, acceleration) only when quality gates pass. Bounded change per tick; skips when physio already tightens ISF strongly. Requires dynamic sensitivity. Off by default. DynISF trajectory: shadow only When on, logs the would-be ISF multiplier but does not change displayed DynISF. Turn off after you trust the signal in logs. DynISF trajectory: max ISF change per tick Cap on relative ISF adjustment from trajectory (e.g. 0.06 = at most about 6% tighter ISF on a strong rise, or 6% looser on a strong fall). Lower = safer, smaller benefit. TAP-G peak governor When adaptive PK/PD is on, blend the insulin profile peak with the learned PKPD peak for loop peakTime (see research doc TAP_G_PEAK_GOVERNOR_RFC). TAP-G learned peak blend weight 0 = insulin anchor only, 1 = learned PKPD peak only. Default 0.55. Use XDrip One Minute Enable support for XDrip one minute BG values Autodrive V3 authoritative SMB When Autodrive V3 is active and issues a safe SMB/TBR, do not recompute SMB with the legacy MPC/PI blender (prevents post-hypo overshoot). Disable only for debugging. Aggressive-rise SMB floor On a confirmed aggressive rise, guarantee at least the user-defined Autodrive prebolus amount, delivered as a floor on top of the model SMB. Always re-bounded by Autodrive V3 safety (post-hypo, max SMB, IOB headroom, correction aggression). Meal pre-bolus Light snack pre-bolus Effort/activity SMB protection Lower SMB when steps and heart rate show current or recent physical effort, even if no activity was declared in AIMI Context. Protection persists for a while after you stop (post-exercise sensitivity) and is skipped when the signals look like stress rather than exercise. Reduction-only. Hyper trajectory SMB release (HTR) When Autodrive V3 is on, lift V3 micro-bolus using scenario projection and trajectory on credible hyper rise. Trigger is not a fixed 200 mg/dL threshold. Meal-rise front-loader (early SMB) On a corroborated meal rise (tree = NEED_MORE_INSULIN, BG above target, rising), let Harmonia apply the early SMB lift even when sensor confidence is low — instead of waiting for established hyper. Only ever softens the authority (never a hard bolus); real hypo, free-fall and safety blocks are never overridden. Off by default: it overrides the sensor-confidence gate. Fix the sensor source first if you can. Sensor confidence: CGM-first Base sensor confidence on the CGM source and signal, not on wearable/health data availability. The old formula let a missing watch collapse sensor confidence and block Harmonia/RBT all day even with a good CGM. When on, a native/filtered CGM is trusted and an unknown source stays cautious rather than fully blocking. This raises dosing authority, so it is off by default. Meal-confirmed early release For undeclared meals: once a meal is confirmed and rising, let the loop reach your configured maximum SMB and basal early, instead of holding back until the high is already established. It only lifts the internal safety floor toward the meal path while blood glucose is climbing, stays within your max SMB, max basal and max IOB, and automatically hands back to the cautious floor once the peak is passed, insulin has stacked, or the rise stops. Real lows and post-hypo protection are never overridden. This raises early dosing, so it is off by default. HTR aggressive floors Raises HTR SMB floors ~15%% when scenario confirms hyper rise. Use only if default release feels too weak. Recursive belief tree (shadow export) Build multi-scale belief tree each loop and export recursive_belief (and physiological_patterns when the physio assistant is on) to AIMI_Decisions.jsonl. Required before RBT authority. Recursive belief tree authority When on, RBT resolves SMB demand and Traj-Bridge suppression from cross-scale tensions (replaces parallel HTR when release authority is active). Enable only after shadow JSONL review. RBT wavelet belief (experimental) Haar 3-band BG decomposition for micro/meso/macro leaves. Off by default. HTR established deviation (mg/dL above target) 0 = TDD-scaled default (~80). Deviation above target for ESTABLISHED tier. HTR deep deviation (mg/dL above target) 0 = TDD-scaled default (~120). Deviation above target for DEEP plateau tier.
High BG threshold (mg/dL) Defines \"high\" for hyper severity classification, trajectory release, physiological phase, scenario projection, and exercise overrides. Used across multiple non-T3C subsystems.
Max adaptive basal multiplier Upper cap for the neural basal multiplier (1.0 = no effect, 2.0 = up to 2× profile basal). Lower if basal increases are too aggressive.
Straight-line tube (tuning) Tube: minimum predicted BG floor (mg/dL) Robust hypo constraint: SMB cap scale is only allowed if min predicted BG minus estimated SMB effect stays at or above this value. Tube: hyper band above target (mg/dL) Eventual BG above target + this band triggers stronger pull toward larger SMB caps (within the hypo tube). Tube: aggressiveness 1.0 = default. Higher = more correction appetite (stronger hyper pull, less command smoothing). Lower = gentler caps. Tube: max basal trim (fraction) When SMB caps are reduced, also scale profile basal and max daily basal by up to this fraction (0 = off). Floor 0.88 applied internally. Tube: kappa safety margin Inflates estimated BG drop per unit SMB (0 = nominal). Use 0.05–0.15 if you want a more conservative tube.
Governance: hypo rate to enter HOLD Fraction of recent samples with BG below the hypo threshold required to enter conservative HOLD (0–1). Lower = harder to trigger. Governance: hypo rate to exit HOLD Must stay below this (and no severe sample) to leave HOLD after hysteresis. Should be lower than enter rate. Governance: hypo BG threshold (mg/dL) Post-sample BG below this counts toward hypo rate in the rolling governance window. Governance: severe hypo BG (mg/dL) Any sample at or below this uses the stricter severe tier floors/decays. Kept strictly below the hypo threshold. HOLD: basal scaling floor (rate tier) Minimum universal basal scaling factor while HOLD applies without a severe sample in the window. HOLD: basal decay per update (rate tier) Each learning update multiplies basal scaling by this value during HOLD (rate tier). Must be < 1. HOLD: T3C aggressiveness floor (rate tier) Minimum T3C aggressiveness factor during HOLD (rate tier). HOLD: T3C aggressiveness decay (rate tier) Multiplicative decay per update for aggressiveness during HOLD (rate tier). HOLD: basal scaling floor (severe tier) Used when at least one sample in the window is at or below the severe hypo BG. HOLD: basal decay (severe tier) Basal scaling multiplicative decay per update during HOLD when severe tier applies. HOLD: T3C aggressiveness floor (severe tier) Minimum aggressiveness when severe hypo tier applies. HOLD: T3C aggressiveness decay (severe tier) Aggressiveness decay per update when severe tier applies. Governance: anticipation lookback (samples) How many recent learning samples (typically 5 min apart) are used to score short-horizon prediction relief. Rounded to a whole number. Governance: anticipation margin above hypo (mg/dL) Minimum predicted BG must be at least hypo threshold plus this margin to count as recovery-oriented for relief. Governance: anticipation hypo dampening When relief is high, weighted hypo rate for HOLD enter/exit is multiplied by (1 minus this fraction times relief). 0 disables hypo dampening from predictions. Governance: anticipation HOLD decay softening Caps how much HOLD basal/aggressiveness decay is eased toward neutral when prediction relief is high. 0 leaves decay unchanged by anticipation.
Ketoacidosis Protection Enables a small safety TBR instead of 0 TBR to reduce the ketoacidosis risk. Variable strategy? If activated the small safety TBR kicks in when IOB is in negative range as if no basal insulin has been delivered for half hour. If deactivated every Zero Temp is replaced with the small TBR. Quantity of the safety TBR [%] Default: 10

Supports crossing midnight (IdleStart > IdleEnd). + (wake up later) → longer night window - (wake up earlier) → shorter night windowb Amplifies the sensitivity boost when movement is detected. + → greater ISF increase during activity (activityRatio decreases more sharply, more insulin) - → weaker effect, smoother transition Increases ISF protection during inactivity. + → greater reduction in insulin during inactivity (activityRatio increases more sharply) - → weaker effect

Basal anti-whiplash (slew limit) Limit how fast the basal rate can rise each cycle to smooth out over-corrections. Basal cuts stay instant for hypo safety; meal and forced-boost paths are exempt. Prediction: endogenous reversion Stop the pkpd eventual prediction from sticking at the 39 mg/dL floor once insulin is spent, letting counter-regulation drift it back toward a low-normal. Affects the eventual only; the hypo-protection floor is unchanged. Prediction: learned insulin kinetics Shape the glucose prediction curves with the adaptive PK/PD learned DIA and peak instead of the fixed insulin profile, so eventual and minPred reflect how your insulin actually acts. Falls back to the profile kinetics when the learner is off or its values are out of range. Basal channel: honour SMB safety holds When a safety rule zeroes the SMB, also block the automatic T3C/Harmonia basal channels instead of letting them take over, and keep the adaptive learner reduction on the rate they propose. Can only lower the automatic temp basal, never raise it. Manual meal modes keep their configured rate. Basal channel: project glucose before correcting Size the temp basal on where glucose is heading over the insulin action window, as a single distance from target, instead of adding a separate trend term that outweighed the distance term 36 to 1. Unchanged when glucose is steady; a rise no longer alone drives several times profile basal. Basal channel: final safety limits Re-check three limits on the temp basal after every multiplier has been applied, instead of before them: hold at profile basal when both glucose and the prediction are below target, while post-hypo recovery is active, or when insulin on board is negative without a rise. Can only lower the rate, never raise it. Manual meal modes are exempt.
Scale ISF by the percentage factor below during confirmed meals to appear more insulin-sensitive and reduce dosing. Apply a time-of-day sine-model ISF adjustment to reflect natural insulin sensitivity variation across 24 hours. Keep Boost active even when a high temporary target is set (e.g. exercise mode); otherwise Boost disables on high TT. Compute dynamic ISF from 24 h total daily dose instead of the profile sensitivity value only. Allow Boost to adjust the sensitivity ratio from UAM / COB feedback; turn off to freeze the ratio at 1.0 for troubleshooting. Use glucose values from any source (including xDrip) for Boost calculations, not only the configured primary CGM. Apply a night-mode BG target offset to reduce insulin delivery during the configured night window. Exit night mode when carbs-on-board is present, treating the COB as a signal that the user is awake and eating. Exit night mode when a low temporary target is set, treating it as a signal that the user is awake and managing. Let the HR/steps sleep detector automatically engage night mode instead of relying only on the fixed time window. Pull heart rate data from Android Health Connect to supplement the live CIQ/watch HR feed. Allow the Boost plugin to run on dev builds that are not tagged as a supported release version. Use V5 meal-hypothesis dosing to control SMB amounts; when OFF, V5 shadows only without affecting actual delivery. Lower the BG target before an anticipated meal (detected by the meal-hypothesis engine) to pre-load insulin. Permit a CONFIRMED meal hypothesis immediately (skip OBSERVING) when COB is present or velocity is very high. Confirm meal hypotheses more aggressively — shortens the OBSERVING phase to speed up dosing escalation. Apply a composed safety floor to meal dosing: never dose below what a hypo-corrected basal would add. Allocate additional aggression budget when BG velocity is high, letting V5 dose more during fast rises. Apply a post-exercise recovery window with adjusted targets and SMB scaling after detected exercise ends. Run a parallel activity-load forecast (inactivity ISF penalty) without affecting dosing, for comparison. Still apply autosens ratio even when TDD is unavailable, falling back to the profile sensitivity adjustment. Incorporate heart-rate data into the Boost algorithm for sleep/wake and stress detection.
